faqs.question: What is Civil Engineering meaning?
faqs.answer: The design, construction, and maintenance of the physically-built and naturally-made environment, including public works such as roads, bridges, canals, dams, airports, sewage systems, pipelines, building structural elements, and trains, fall under the broad category of Civil Engineering field . To address potential issues and build secure and effective structures, civil engineers use their expertise in Maths, Science, Computers, and Engineering. They work on many different types of projects, ranging from little bridges to enormous buildings. So as the way of thinking changes, universities are bringing up a new generation of civil engineers who can meet the challenges of the environment initially. This involves incorporating sustainable practices (utilizing green building materials and energy-efficient designs) in order to minimize the environmental impact of a building construction. It is also highlighting issues relating to the environment, at its very core is ensuring that construction projects have as little impact on the environment as possible. Our world is actually built on the accomplishments of this field. Building shelters to protect oneself from the weather and using tree trunks as makeshift bridges to cross rivers in the past, everything falls under the umbrella of the Civil Engg. discipline. Our ancestors did not indulge in any such calculations, but they were basically using the principles of Civil Engineering courses to find solutions to their problems.

faqs.answer: The Civil Engineering course duration differs on the basis of the course level at which you're planning to pursue the course. For UG courses like BTech/B.E in Civil Engineering , the general duration is 4 years while for PG courses you need to invest at least 2 years . You can also go for a 3 year Civil Engineering Diploma after Class 10 or short term certifications that last 1 year or less . For students interested in a PhD in Civil Engineering , the time span is 3 to 5 years in general. Know more about - Engineering Courses

faqs.question: Why study Civil Engineering courses after 12th?
faqs.answer: Some of the key advantages of pursuing Civil Engineering courses after 12th are mentioned below. Civil Engineers are always in demand because of rapid urbanization and increasing technological advancements which further fuel infrastructural needs. The construction sector is continuously evolving and never out of demand, hence the need for civil engineers is more with the chances of layoffs being less likely to emerge. Civil Engineers leave a lasting impact on the society with their involvement in the construction of roads, buildings, airports, etc., where project planning may take up several years and technical expertise. This field offers people with immense learning opportunities owing to everyday technological innovations and increase in individual demands which requires creativity and an innovative mindset. Civil engineers hold a valuable and respected position in the society for their contribution towards improvement of communities through structural advancements. know more about - Civil Engineering Courses

faqs.question: What are the eligibility criteria to get admission to Civil Engineering?
faqs.answer: The eligibility requirements for admission into Civil Engineering courses in India can be stated as Minimum Qualification: You must have completed your 12th standard (or equivalent) from a recognised school/college. Science Stream: Majority of institutions need you to have completed Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics popularly known as PCM stream. Some of the colleges may accept the PCMB (including Biology) as well. However, these options are rare. Minimum Marks: The minimum marks requirement differs from institute to institute and according to the category of the student applying for a reservation. In general, an average of minimum 50 percent marks in PCM subjects is expected ( 45 percent for SC/ST/OBC categories ). Entrance Exams: In order to get admission in top institutes like IITs and NITs, you need to qualify JEE Mains and JEE Advanced for BTech courses and GATE for MTech courses. These are the national level exams for Engineering courses in general. Other than them there many state level and university specific exams also like WBJEE, TS EAMCET, BITSAT and VITEEE . All the best!

faqs.question: Do I have to give any entrance exam for admission to BTech Civil Engineering course?
faqs.answer: A lot of B Tech Civil Engineering colleges and universities admit students taking into consideration their Class 12 marks and take extra rounds like the GD or PI in such cases. Having said that, most of the top Civil Engineering colleges in India provide admission on the basis of valid entrance test scores. The IITs and the NITs need valid JEE Main and JEE Advanced scores, for giving admission to students to the BTech Civil Engg. course. So, you should go to the official college website and see the admission guidelines to see if they provide entrance/merit-based admissions or give 50-50 weightage to both parameters.

faqs.question: What is taught in the Civil Engineering subject: Air Pollution Control and Management?
faqs.answer: Dear candidate, The Air Pollution Control and Management subject basically teaches you about the environmental impact of air emissions that occur at the time of construction of any of the small-scale or large-scale infrastructural projects, the ways in which you can control those pollutants by using different techniques and also how modern technological advancements have led to the introduction of air pollution control systems for the benefit of people residing in nearby areas. It is extremely important to study this subject well so that you can use the protocols well in advance to avoid extreme environmental impact and ensure effective project execution in a timely manner. Hope this cleared your doubt. Have a good day.

faqs.answer: The BTech in Civil Engg. syllabus taught in classes is a mix of both core and elective subjects. There is no scope for customization in core subjects as those are compulsory for you to study in each semester. The core subjects give you a strong foundational base of the Civil Engineering field so that you can become job-ready for the future. Talking about the elective subjects, you can pick the subjects according to your interests and convenience, something you find intriguing, easy to grasp, and the ones that align with your career goals. So, you do have that chance of some sort of customization via the elective subject choices in the BTech Civil Engineering syllabus.

content.text: With the rapid use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and other technological advancements taking place in the digitalized world we are living in at present, several emerging trends are revamping the career pathway for Civil Engineering jobs in India as well, making project execution quicker and smarter.

items: Building Information Modelling(BIM):A 3D-model smart digital software technology that enables the engineer to design and manage the physical and functional outlook of building structures.

Geographic Information Systems (GIS):GIS Tools come in handy for site analysis, and systematic land planning as well as allocation for the purpose of avoiding any future complexities with regard to infrastructure positioning.

Green Building Materials:These construction materials are eco-friendly and ensure efficient use of energy resources keeping in mind the pressing global environmental concerns. For instance, recycled wood and steel, bio-based insulators, and so on, can be used to reduce environmental strain.

Renewable Energy Integration:This process involves fusing renewable energy sources to the electric grid systems so as to minimize carbon emissions and other pollutants responsible for air pollution and deterioration of air quality index.

Advanced Robotics:Advanced robot technology has led to a massive surge in productivity in the given field, reducing labor costs and time-consuming manual tasks. Advanced robots perform automatic procedures such as construction site inspections via drone devices, and masonry and concrete casting tasks through robotic arms fitted with advanced sensor systems.

Structural Monitoring and Assessment (SHM) Tools:These tools instantaneously provide information about the present condition of structures further enabling better maintenance, risk analysis, and timely action to avoid casualty.

Disaster Management:Advanced sensor algorithms and satellite networks help detect future environmental calamities that include earthquakes, floods, and more, which ensure timely evacuation in cases of emergency and a good plan of action.

During the recent placements, top global companies such as Google, Amazon, Microsoft, Deloitte, and TCS visited the campus. The average salary package offered was 9 LPA and the highest salary package offered was 51 LPA.
